Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit that later turn brown with a yellow halo.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Copper-based bactericide sprays (e.g., copper hydroxide) applied at first sign of disease.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.organic_alternative: Copper soap fungicide/bactericide; remove and destroy infected plant debris.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use disease-free seed, avoid overhead watering, rotate crops, avoid working in fields when plants are wet.

Pepper__bell___healthy.prevention: Continue regular watering, balanced fertilization, and monitoring for early signs of pests or disease.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target-like pattern) on older leaves first.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb, applied every 7-10 days once symptoms appear.
Potato___Early_blight.organic_alternative: Copper-based fungicide or neem oil spray; remove infected lower leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops (avoid planting potatoes/tomatoes in the same spot yearly), ensure good spacing for airflow, avoid overhead irrigation.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves that rapidly turn brown/black; white fungal growth on leaf undersides in humid conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Copper-based fungicide (copper oxychloride) or chlorothalonil, applied immediately at first symptoms - this disease spreads fast.
Potato___Late_blight.organic_alternative: Copper fungicide sprays; remove and destroy infected plants immediately to stop spread.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Avoid overhead watering, ensure good air circulation, plant resistant varieties, destroy volunteer potato plants.

Potato___healthy.prevention: Continue regular watering, balanced fertilization, and monitoring for early signs of pests or disease.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, greasy-looking spots on leaves, stems, and fruit.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.treatment: Copper-based bactericide sprays combined with mancozeb for better control.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.organic_alternative: Copper soap spray; remove and destroy infected leaves and debris.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds/transplants, avoid overhead watering, rotate crops every 2-3 years.

Tomato_Early_blight.symptoms: Dark spots with concentric rings on older/lower leaves, which then yellow and drop.
Tomato_Early_blight.treatment: Fungicides containing chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper compounds.
Tomato_Early_blight.organic_alternative: Neem oil or copper fungicide spray; mulch around base to prevent soil splash onto leaves.
Tomato_Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, stake plants for airflow, water at the base rather than overhead, remove lower infected leaves promptly.

Tomato_Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular, water-soaked patches on leaves that turn brown/black quickly; white mold on undersides in humid weather.
Tomato_Late_blight.treatment: Copper-based fungicide or chlorothalonil applied immediately - this disease can destroy a crop within days in humid weather.
Tomato_Late_blight.organic_alternative: Copper fungicide spray; remove and destroy all infected plants immediately, do not compost.
Tomato_Late_blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, avoid overhead watering, ensure good spacing and airflow, monitor closely during humid/wet weather.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green/yellow spots on upper leaf surface with olive-green to grayish-purple mold on the underside.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.treatment: Fungicides containing chlorothalonil or copper compounds; improve ventilation especially in greenhouses.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.organic_alternative: Copper fungicide spray; increase spacing and ventilation to reduce humidity around plants.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.prevention: Reduce humidity around plants (greenhouse ventilation), avoid overhead watering, remove and destroy infected leaves.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small, circular spots with dark borders and gray/tan centers, usually starting on lower leaves.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Fungicides containing chlorothalonil or copper, applied at first sign and repeated every 7-10 days.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.organic_alternative: Copper fungicide spray; remove infected lower leaves and mulch to prevent soil splash.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Rotate crops, avoid overhead watering, stake/prune for airflow, clean up plant debris at season end.

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.cause: Pest infestation (Tetranychus urticae, a mite - not a disease)
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.symptoms: Fine yellow/white stippling on leaves, fine webbing on undersides in heavy infestations, leaves may bronze and dry out.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.treatment: Miticide sprays (e.g., abamectin) or insecticidal soap; horticultural oils also help.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.organic_alternative: Neem oil or insecticidal soap spray; introduce predatory mites as biological control; spray plants with water to dislodge mites.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.prevention: Keep plants well-watered (mites thrive in dry, dusty conditions), avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer, monitor regularly.

Tomato__Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown lesions with concentric rings (target-like) on leaves, stems, and fruit.
Tomato__Target_Spot.organic_alternative: Copper fungicide spray; remove and destroy infected plant material.
Tomato__Target_Spot.prevention: Improve air circulation, avoid overhead watering, rotate crops, remove plant debris after harvest.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.cause: Viral (Tomato yellow leaf curl virus, spread by whiteflies)
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaves, stunted growth, reduced fruit production.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.treatment: No cure once infected - focus shifts to controlling the whitefly vector with insecticides (e.g., imidacloprid) and removing infected plants.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.organic_alternative: Insecticidal soap or neem oil to control whiteflies; use reflective mulches to repel whiteflies; remove and destroy infected plants.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.prevention: Use virus-resistant tomato varieties, control whitefly populations, use row covers on young plants, remove weeds that can host the virus.

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light/dark green pattern on leaves, leaf curling, stunted growth, distorted fruit.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: No cure once infected - remove and destroy infected plants to prevent spread; disinfect tools between plants.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.organic_alternative: No organic treatment cures the virus; focus on removing infected plants and sanitizing equipment.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use certified virus-free seeds, wash hands and disinfect tools between handling plants, control aphids which can spread the virus, avoid tobacco use near plants (virus can spread from tobacco products).

Tomato_healthy.prevention: Continue regular watering, balanced fertilization, and monitoring for early signs of pests or disease.
